findings.title: argon2i_32 with nb_blocks < 2 causes heap buffer overflow in crypto_argon2
findings.evidence: argon2i_32 (c_monocypher.pyx:322) accepts any unsigned int nb_blocks, stores it in config.nb_blocks (line 328), allocates work_area = malloc(nb_blocks * 1024) (line 345), and calls crypto_argon2 (line 347) with no lower-bound check, even though monocypher.h:160 documents the precondition nb_blocks >= 8 * nb_lanes. The C implementation derives segment_size = nb_blocks/1/4 and lane_size = 4*segment_size (monocypher.c:752-753) but unconditionally fills the first two blocks of each lane: FOR_T(u32, i, 0, 2) load64_le_buf(blocks[l*lane_size + i].a, hash_area, 128) (monocypher.c:776-781). With nb_blocks = 1 the work area is only 1024 bytes yet blocks[1] is written at offset 1024..2047, a 1024-byte heap overflow; with nb_blocks = 0 malloc(0) succeeds and 2048 bytes are written past it. Reachable by any Python caller, e.g. argon2i_32(1, 1, b'password', b'salt'), and by any application that forwards an untrusted or config-supplied KDF cost parameter into this API: heap metadata/corruption occurs before any error can be raised.

findings.title: argon2i_32 with nb_blocks 2-3 causes 1 KiB out-of-bounds read hashed into the output
findings.evidence: For nb_blocks in {2, 3} and nb_lanes = 1, crypto_argon2 computes segment_size = nb_blocks/1/4 = 0 and lane_size = segment_size*4 = 0 (monocypher.c:752-753), so all segment fill loops iterate zero times. After the pass loop the code executes blk *last_block = blocks + lane_size - 1 (monocypher.c:902), which underflows to blocks - 1, and store64_le_buf(final_block, last_block->a, 128) (monocypher.c:911) reads 1024 bytes located before the malloc'ed work_area (heap chunk headers and neighboring allocation data). extended_hash then absorbs that out-of-bounds data into the 32-byte digest returned by argon2i_32 (c_monocypher.pyx:347-352). Reachable with a plain call such as argon2i_32(2, 1, b'password', b'salt'); consequence is an out-of-bounds heap read (ASan/valgrind abort, potential crash) and a KDF output that depends on unrelated heap contents.

findings.title: argon2i_32 with nb_iterations = 0 reads uninitialized work-area memory
findings.evidence: nb_iterations is copied unvalidated into config.nb_passes (c_monocypher.pyx:329), although monocypher.h:161 documents the precondition nb_passes >= 1. With nb_iterations = 0 the fill loop FOR_T(u32, pass, 0, config.nb_passes) (monocypher.c:802) and all slice/segment loops (803-895) are skipped; only the two seed blocks written at monocypher.c:776-782 are initialized. The final block blocks[lane_size-1] is therefore uninitialized malloc memory when it is read at monocypher.c:902/911 and hashed into the returned digest (c_monocypher.pyx:347). Reachable via argon2i_32(8, 0, b'password', b'salt'); the KDF output is then derived from uninitialized heap contents (use of uninitialized resource), providing no CPU-hardening whatsoever.

findings.title: Unchecked malloc result in argon2i_32 can pass NULL work_area into crypto_argon2
findings.evidence: work_area = malloc((<size_t> nb_blocks) * (<size_t> 1024)) at c_monocypher.pyx:345 does not check for NULL. nb_blocks may be any uint32 value (Cython accepts 0..0xffffffff for the assignment at line 328), so e.g. argon2i_32(0xffffffff, 1, b'p', b's') requests a ~4 TiB allocation, which fails on typical systems. The NULL pointer is passed directly to crypto_argon2 (line 347), which immediately writes blocks[l*lane_size + i] (monocypher.c:781) through it, causing an access violation that terminates the Python interpreter (denial of service) rather than raising MemoryError; the finally block only frees the (NULL) pointer.

findings.title: blake2b/blake2b_keyed_init: key longer than 128 bytes causes stack buffer overflow
findings.evidence: blake2b (c_monocypher.pyx:276-282) forwards the raw length of the Python key to crypto_blake2b_keyed (line 281), and Blake2b.__init__ does the same to crypto_blake2b_keyed_init (line 297); Cython performs no length check when converting bytes to const uint8_t* and no bound is enforced on len(key). crypto_blake2b_keyed -> crypto_blake2b_keyed_init then executes u8 key_block[128] = {0}; COPY(key_block, key, key_size); (monocypher.c:545-546), where COPY is a byte loop, so any key_size > 128 writes attacker-supplied key bytes past a 128-byte stack buffer inside the callee frame, corrupting saved state/return addresses. BLAKE2 permits key_size <= 64 and the wrapper's own docstring says 'optional 32-byte key', but nothing rejects longer keys: blake2b(b'msg', key=b'A'*1024) is accepted and smashes the stack. Reachable whenever an application uses caller-influenced key material (e.g. a passphrase) for keyed hashing.
